newsitem.title: USA: Dlr closes higher in US but below new high vs yen.
newsitem.headline: Dlr closes higher in US but below new high vs yen.

text.p: The dollar ended higher, shaking off weaker U.S. asset prices to recover from profit-taking that toppled it from its best level against the yen in nearly four years, dealer said.
Dollar/yen hit 120.15 in Tokyo but dollar/mark failed to reignite the rally which touched a 31-month high Thursday.

After the overnight decline, several attempts to push the dollar back above 1.63 marks and 119 yen were checked by a decline in U.S. asset prices. But the dollar got late support after the Dow Jones stock index recouped some of its early 95 point decline, dealers said.

"They sold (the dollar) down, now the Dow has sort of recovered a little bit, so people are buying it back," said Jeffrey Yu, senior dealer at Sanwa Bank Ltd in New York. "There is no rhyme or reason right now for the market."
The dollar ended at 118.85/95 yen, up from 118.67/72 yen at the open. It closed at 1.6285/90 marks, up from 1.6260/65 marks.
U.S. Treasury bonds fell more than half a point early on Friday before recovering somewhat. Stocks ended the day with a 59 point loss.

"People were taken aback by the sort of -- out of nowhere -- very sharp weakness in bonds ... they were starting to wack stocks again and the dollar came under some pressure," said Alfonso Alejo, a vice president at Sakura Bank Ltd.
The dollar rose above 120 yen in Tokyo after Japanese officials said the falling stock market and weak yen would not stall Japan's economy.
But the dollar later succumbed to talk the Bank of Japan (BOJ) had sold dollars for yen and remarks by other government officials.
"We came off and we got some more comments ... that an excessively weak yen is not in the interest of the Japanese either," said Ben Strauss, assistant vice president at Bank Julius Baer and Co.
"Although people are still bullish on the dollar overall, its in a consolidation phase," Yu added. "So the key now ... is people are really looking into the BOJ's real intentions," he added.
A Japanese wire service later reported a senior Finance Ministry official rejected speculation that the central bank conducted the operation in the currency market.

Comments by Masayuki Matsushima, director of the central bank's research and statistics department were echoed by Japan's Vice Minister of economic planning, who said the recent weakness of the yen was having no major negative impact on Japan's economy.
However, a senior Ministry of Finance official left the opposite impression by adhering to the line repeated often by finance officials warning against yen volatility.
"Like excessive appreciation ... an excessive depreciaton of the yen is not welcome," the official told reporters in Tokyo.
But the official declined to say at what level the yen would be considered excessively weak.
In other trade, the dollar closed at 1.4055/65 Swiss francs, up from 1.4025/35 at the open.
It rose to Canadian $1.3485/90 from C$1.3483/88.
The pound rose to $1.6290/95 from $1.6285/95.
The Australian dollar fell to $0.7721/26 from $0.7730/40.
((--Alden Bentley, 212 859 1667))
